sections.heading: Summary
sections.markdown: Miriel, Pastor of Vows** is an NPC in Elden Ring.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.markdown:
Miriel, Pastor of Vows is the steward of the Church of Vows in eastern Liurnia of the Lakes. A gigantic tortoise wearing a large white mitre, Miriel is a gentle soul who will happily assist the Tarnished on their journey.

Well-versed in both sorceries and incantations, Miriel can be given scrolls as well as prayerbooks, and will readily teach new spells to the player for an appropriate fee. Miriel's true passion is for the miracle of Absolution, which he believes will mend the world.

Miriel also serves as an excellent source of lore on Rennala, Queen of the Full Moon, and her former husband, Radagon of the Golden Order. Exhausting Miriel's dialogue can direct the player toward secrets that advance multiple questlines.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.markdown: - Miriel is the most reliable cleric NPC for prayerbooks, since he never moves away from the church, accepts all types of books and only becomes unavailable once during the Bell Bearing Hunter invasion.

sections.markdown: The **Moonlight Altar** is a subregion of the Lands Between in Elden Ring. It is located above Liurnia of the Lakes and can only be accessed after advancing Ranni the Witch's questline.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.markdown:
A plateau on the east side of Liurnia bathed in the light of the Dark Moon. It is accessible only by passing through Ainsel River and the Lake of Rot and defeating Astel, Naturalborn of the Void. The lift which leads to the Moonlight Altar is sealed, and can only be accessed by obtaining the Dark Moon Ring from the treasure chest in Rennala's library in the Academy of Raya Lucaria.

The plateau, which sits above the Village of the Albinaurics, is the site of the Cathedral of Manus Celes, a large, ruined church. The Ringleader's Evergaol, housing the ringleader of the Black Knife Assassins, can also be found here.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.markdown: The **Night of Black Knives** (黒き刃の陰謀の夜, *Kuroki Yaiba no Inbō no Yoru*) was an event mentioned in Elden Ring. It involved the theft of Destined Death and the assassination of Godwyn the Golden, a son of Queen Marika the Eternal. It would serve as the catalyst of the conflict known as The Shattering.

sections.heading: Prelude
sections.markdown:
Although the conspirators behind it remained unknown to the wider world, it was in fact orchestrated by Lunar Princess Ranni as she was looking for a way to free herself from the control of the Two Fingers.
Ranni, who sought to change her fate, stole a piece of the Rune of Death from Maliketh, who served as the guardian of the rune. With the stolen fragment, Ranni proceeded to imbue the Black Knives of Numen Assassins, all of them being women from the Eternal Cities with ties to Marika, with the powers of Destined Death.

On the same night, Ranni gifted her brother, Praetor Rykard, with the Blasphemous Claw, a rock engraved with traces of the Rune of Death, as a reward for helping her in the plot and to make Rykard able to challenge Maliketh on the day of his blasphemy.

sections.heading: Assassination
sections.markdown:
Wishing to shed her Empyrean body but preserve her spirit, she knew that the spirit of someone else had to die as well. On the night of the plot, the assassins arrived in Leyndell, the Royal Capital, and slew Godwyn the Golden, carving the Cursemark of Death into his flesh. The Cursemark was supposed to form a circle; however, as Ranni perished in the same moment as Godwyn, the mark was split into two half-wheels. Godwyn's soul alone perished, while Ranni became the first Demigod to die in the flesh.

Immediately following the assassination, the Black Knives fled the capital. Tiche, the daughter of the Black Knife Ringleader Alecto, died protecting her mother during the escape.

sections.heading: Aftermath
sections.markdown:
Godwyn's body was interred in the Deeproot Depths at the base of the Erdtree's roots, where he mutated and deformed into the being that would become known as the Prince of Death. Later, the traces of the Rune of Death used to slay him spread through the network of Greattree roots that span the Lands Between, taking the form of Deathroot, the source of Those Who Live in Death.

Ranni, whose Empyrean body perished upon the carving of the Cursemark, transferred her soul into a doll modeled after her mentor. She maintained a low profile following the Night of Black Knives, and it is unknown whether her death was widely known.

Following the Night of Black Knives, the Elden Ring was shattered by Queen Marika. As a result, the great war known as The Shattering ensued.

In the aftermath of the Shattering, a Tarnished known as Fia, the Deathbed Companion, came into contact with the soulless body of Godwyn. Fia sought the two half-wheels, wishing to reunite them and produce a Mending Rune, which could introduce Those Who Live in Death to the Elden Ring. During this time, another Tarnished named Rogier began to study the Night of Black Knives, bringing him into contact with Fia.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.markdown: Noble Page** is an enemy in Elden Ring.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.markdown:
Pages are servants to nobility. They came to serve by birth into obscurity, regardless of aptitude or volition. They wear fine clothes as to avoid any undue shame in their master's way, and sack-like hoods befitting their unremarkable servitude. High Pages are selected for special privileges by their master.

Pages are dexterous opponents, capable of weaving in and out of attacks before either lunging with their Estoc or firing a bolt from their off-hand Soldier's Crossbow. They rely on the element of surprise or ranged engagements, as their physical defenses are lacking. High Pages wield a Pulley Crossbow loaded with Perfumer's Bolts instead.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.markdown: Misbegotten Warriors** are enemies in Elden Ring. They are a powerful variant of the Misbegotten enemy and often appear as bosses, including Leonine Misbegotten and Misbegotten Crusader.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.markdown: Misbegotten Warriors are feral humanoids marked by bestial traits—claws, fangs, feathered wings, serpentine tails, and a thick red lion’s mane. Like other Misbegotten, their appearance is seen as punishment for ancient contact with the primordial Crucible. They are nimble and aggressive, wildly swinging weighty Iron Greatswords and leaping into the air.

sections.heading: Moveset
sections.markdown: Misbegotten Warriors deal Standard damage. They are highly aggressive and mobile, and finding safe openings to counterattack can be difficult. They can enter a buffed state with glowing red eyes by using Barbaric Roar.

sections.heading: Background
sections.markdown:
See also: Perfumer Tricia (Boss)*

A Misbegotten Warrior fought alongside Perfumer Tricia at the end of the Unsightly Catacombs. Tricia, a healer devoted to treating impure creatures, appears to have allied with the Misbegotten.

sections.heading: Background

See also: Crucible Knight*

A Misbegotten Warrior fought in the plaza of Redmane Castle when the Radahn Festival is not active. When reduced to half health, a Crucible Knight joins the fight.

sections.heading: Background

Miranda Sprouts are small, mobile, flesh eating flowers that cause a variety of Status Effects with their pollen.

They are often found around the larger Miranda Blossoms, and are said to descend from Miranda, maiden of the Flower Crucible who are also their namesake.

They are very weak to Fire and since they are slow and short-ranged in their attacks they are easily handled with a ranged weapon or consumables.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.markdown: Miner** is an enemy in Elden Ring.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.markdown:
Miners are laborers with skin like cracked stone, found in mines and tunnels throughout the Lands Between. Their stonelike skin grants resistance to slashing attacks, but they are vulnerable to Strike-based damage.

They wield mining tools such as Pickaxes and Explosive Stones, once used for rock blasting. Some carry lanterns that can spew fire, while others haul sacks of rocks, hurling them alongside Explosive Stones and Poisoned Stones. These stones were originally pest control tools, though the Miners have long forgotten how to craft them.

Some miners are failed scholars, working in crystal tunnels as sorcerer-miners. They wield Digger's Staffs that double as mining tools, enhancing Stonedigger sorceries like Shatter Earth. Others may hurl Glintstone Scraps during combat.

sections.heading: Variant Description
sections.markdown: Miners typically found in caves and mining tunnels. Most wield pickaxes, while some carry lanterns that they can use to spew fire. Some have sacks of rocks on their backs, and will throw rocks as well as Explosive Stones and Poisoned Stones, which are employed as tools for pest extermination, although the Miners have long forgotten how to craft them.

sections.heading: Variant Description
sections.markdown: Sorcerer-miners who work in crystal tunnels. They wield glintstone staves which serve as mining tools, enhancing the power of Stonedigger sorceries which mark these miners as failed scholars. Some may also throw Glintstone Scraps in combat.

sections.markdown: Mausoleum Knights** is enemies in Elden Ring.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.markdown:
The Mausoleum Knights of Castle Sol willingly beheaded themselves to serve their masters in Death, a self-inflicted curse that bound their souls to the land. In doing so, they became phantasmal guardians of the Wandering Mausoleums—enormous, tolling belfries interring the soulless cadavers of dead Demigods. Lhutel the Headless, leader of the Mausoleum Knights, sacrificed her life to continue serving a soulless Demigod until their revival, earning her the hero's honor of Erdtree Burial.

The Knights commanded the Mausoleum Soldiers and Mausoleum Foot Soldiers, and maintained a large presence in Tombsward, northern Liurnia, and around the Nameless Eternal City in the Deeproot Depths. A detachment at Noklateo, the Shrouded City included Headless Trolls, Headless Gladiators, and Headless Fallen Hawk Soldiers.

They wore wing-shaped ornaments on their backs to evoke the wicked Deathbirds of old—offspring of the Twinbird who burned death in cold ghostflame to release vengeful spirits. Their crested shields displayed the sun in eclipse, a star that protected the soulless by keeping Destined Death at bay. They bore weapons enrobed in the Prince of Death's black-and-gold flame, inflicting Holy damage and Death Blight buildup, and they hurled phantasmal spears.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.markdown: Minor Erdtrees** are Landmarks in Elden Ring.

sections.heading: Characteristics
sections.markdown: Gargantuan deciduous trees with dense canopies of golden leaves, visible from great distances. The bark of young Minor Erdtrees gives off a golden glow that apparently fades as they reach maturity.

sections.heading: Background
sections.markdown:
The Erdtree's offspring sprouted from its fabled Golden Seeds, scattered across the Lands Between when it sensed the end of its life for the first time.

Queen Marika the Eternal would plant developing Minor Erdtrees at the Minor Erdtree Church, where she would deliver a speech, demanding to abandon blind faith and declaring her intent of inquiring the depths of her Golden Order in an attempt to strengthen its grace through understanding. The order of the Erdtree Guardians would be established to protect the Erdtree's offspring through a pact with it. Talismans depicting the Erdtree seed, once believed as something that could not exist, were crafted to increase the powers of its blessed sap. Perfumers developed wondrous physicks using the crystal tears that were slowly collected in basins at the feet of the Minor Erdtrees. Catacombs for Erdtree Burial would be built close to Minor Erdtrees as their roots were once linked together with those of the Erdtree.

Upon the shattering of the Elden Ring, fearing its coming end again, the Erdtree would release new seeds that would start growing into Illusory Trees and deploy Erdtree Avatars to protect its already grown but withering offspring.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.markdown:
- Crystalized Tears for the Flask of Wondrous Physick are commonly acquired at Minor Erdtrees.
- Small collection basins are found at the base of most Minor Erdtrees. They collected hardened sap.
- Teardrop Scarabs often linger near Minor Erdtrees.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.markdown: The **Nomadic Merchants** are a faction in Elden Ring.

sections.heading: Background
sections.markdown:
Long ago, the ancestors of the Nomadic Merchants were spurned by Grace, condemned to a life of endless wandering with no place to settle. Once they had thrived as the Great Caravan, but a maddening disease had followed in their wake. In an effort to bury it, Queen Marika had their people sealed deep beneath the Subterranean Shunning-Grounds. There in the dark, they chanted a curse of despair, calling forth the Frenzied Flame.

Those who remained roamed the Lands Between, bound by a code forbidding them to lament their solitude or seek sympathy, and vowing to show no mercy to any who dared to harm them. These wandering traders searched the realm for their ancestors, and the home that vanished with them.

sections.heading: Characteristics
sections.markdown: A scattered clan of Nomadic Merchants is found all over the Lands Between, often sitting at campfires, sometimes with their Mules nearby. Some can be seen playing a somber melody on stringed instruments. The wares they sell are frequently influenced by or representative of their current locations. Each merchant wears a unique recolor of the basic outfit. The notes of information they offer are marked by colored feathers matching the seller's outfit.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.markdown:
- All nomadic merchants may be attacked and killed for their Bell Bearings. They may mount their mules and ride around or retaliate with the Flame of Frenzy.
- The song played by the nomadic merchants is a simplified version of Midra, Lord of Frenzied Flame's boss theme.

- Nomadic Merchants have several unused musical attacks.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.markdown:
Mind** is one of the main attribute stats in Elden Ring.

The Tarnished's Mind stat directly affects their FP totals. In addition, leveling Mind will also increase Focus, increasing the Tarnished's resistance to Sleep and Madness.

The Tarnished can level Mind by spending Runes at Sites of Grace. Mind has a soft cap of 50 and 60 for increasing FP, and a soft cap of 40 and 60 for increasing Focus, with each derivative stat seeing diminishing returns after reaching these soft caps. Leveling Mind will not begin to see Focus returns until 31 and onwards.

A +0 Flask of Cerulean Tears replenishes 80 FP upon use, equivalent to 9/10 Mind, while a +12 Flask replenishes 220 FP, equivalent to 37/38 Mind.

sections.heading: Increasing Mind
sections.markdown:
- Fingerprint NostrumShadow of the Erdtree: Increases Intelligence by 6 for 90 seconds. Also increases Mind, Faith, and Arcane by 6 and drains 3 HP per second for the same duration.
- Marika's Scarseal/Soreseal grants +3/5 Mind, as well as Faith, Intelligence, and Arcane, but increases damage taken by 10%/15%. Cannot be worn at the same time.
- Navy Hood grants +1 Mind.
- Preceptor's Big Hat grant +3 Mind but decreases Stamina by roughly 9%.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.markdown: A sorcerer's rise in Altus Plateau, in the valley south-west of the Minor Erdtree. An imp statue nearby provides the Mirage Riddle, a map which shows the positions of the crests. Spectral Imps will appear near each crest, and will only stop spawning once the crest has been touched. sections.heading: Summary
sections.markdown:
Messages are an asymetric multiplayer mechanic, returning from many of FromSoftware's previous games, they allow players to potentially influence the gameplay experience of others through the sharing of cryptic, yet helpful hints, deceptive and unhelpful advice, jokes lightening the mood or sharing of one's rejoice of a glorious victory.
Messages are written through the use of the Tarnished's Wizened Finger.

sections.heading: Write Message
sections.markdown:
Players can place down messages in the hopes of them getting rated. Should a message be rated, whether they be applauded or disparaged the player who's message have been rated will get some of their HP restored.

Messages are constructed through the use of filling in two (to potentially six) different slots for preset phrases in the form of three different formats, Templates, Words and Conjunctions (players may also add a Gesture to the message in order to add some extra clarification in terms of directions or just to give the message more personality).

sections.heading: Message Compositions
sections.markdown:
There are four different message compositions the player can chose from each varying the amount of available options.
However the fourth composition is generally the most convenient since it'll still allow a message to be placed even if only the slots that are available in the first three compositions are filled.

sections.heading: Templates
sections.markdown: Templates usually include a section of "****"s, these will be filled in by whatever option the player has selected in the "Words" box.

sections.heading: Words
sections.markdown:
The "Words" box is used to fill in the "****"s of the "Template" section.
There are twelve different categories where the writer can get their words from.

sections.heading: Conjunctions
sections.markdown: Conjunctions become available should the first two "Templates" and "Word" boxes not be enough for the message's clarity and will serve as a transition between the first set of templates and words boxes into the newly revealed second set.

sections.heading: Gestures
sections.markdown:
Adding a Gesture will make a phantom version of the writer perform said gesture while other players are reading the message.
Any Gesture that the player has found on their journey will be available for selection.

sections.heading: Messages Written
sections.markdown: You can leave a total of 10 messages at a time. Once you've made an 11th message the game will automatically remove your oldest message no matter how highly rated it is.

sections.heading: Messages Discovered
sections.markdown: Any messages you've read recently will be stored in this section for later reference and rating. The game can only remember 10 messages at a time though, so the moment you've read your 11th message, the oldest discovered message will be removed.

sections.heading: Rating Score
sections.markdown: Messages will have their icons change over time depending on how many ratings it has received.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.markdown: Nomads** are enemies in Elden Ring.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.markdown:
Nomads are withered, tormented musicians with gold and silver hair whose filthy white robes hang loosely to their frail frames. They play a somber melody on their stringed instruments using bows that terminate in a five-fingered hand. They are the ancestors of Merchant Kalé and the Nomadic Merchants.

They are found exclusively in the Subterranean Shunning-Grounds, between the Cathedral of the Forsaken and the Frenzied Flame Proscription Sites of Grace. A single Nomad can be found playing the nomadic merchant song on his instrument on the way down to the Frenzied Flame Proscription. He will remain non-hostile until the player provokes him by attacking.

Nomads wield the Frenzied Flame, which they release in deadly volleys in combat. They deal Standard and Fire damage and inflict Madness buildup.

sections.heading: Background
sections.markdown:
The nomads once comprised the Great Caravan, a once-thriving tribe of merchants and traders in the Lands Between. However, with the rise of Queen Marika, they found themselves spurned by the Grace of her Erdtree. Like many others, the members of the Great Caravan were left to struggle at the fringes of society. They did not mind their situation, but were deeply unforgiving toward those who would harm them.

A maddening sickness followed the nomads wherever they went, and they were accused of harboring the Flame of Frenzy. Soon, the entire clan was rounded up and confined to a claustrophobic catacombs in the suffocating depths below Leyndell, Royal Capital—buried beneath even the accursed Omen. Immured within the Frenzied Flame Proscription, the nomads chanted a curse of despair, summoning the heretical Three Fingers.

sections.heading: Drops
sections.markdown: Nomads do not drop items upon defeat.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.markdown:
- Nomads are immune to Sleep ailment buildup.
- They share several moves with the surface-dwelling Nomadic Merchants; however, their Frenzied Flame attacks are more potent and they can't cast buffs on themselves with their musical instruments.
- The nomads of the Great Caravan were adverse to settling down, predisposing them to chaos. Their confinement under the Golden Order took away their nomadic lifestyle.
- The Nomads' hand bow and robe cannot be acquired.
- Their attacks can demolish the tents in the area, allowing access to the items underneath.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.markdown:
- The Nomads use a highly detailed animation when playing their instruments. Their fingers accurately slide to the correct spots to produce the notes being played.
- Their immunity to Sleep may be a holdover from a cut iteration of the Nomadic Merchant story that involved St. Trina and Slumber Fog.
- A cut version of Merchant Kalé's questline allowed him to discover the fate of the Great Caravan.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.markdown:
Millicent's sisters** are adopted daughters of Sage Gowry and siblings of Millicent. These red haired girls once sprouted as buds from the Scarlet Aeonia found within the heart of Caelid. They all wear the Traveler's Set and use weapons and skills associated with either aspects of their inadvertent mother Malenia, both her role as the unalloyed blade of Miquella and her looming transformation into the goddess of rot. They all seek to aid their adoptive father in cultivating Millicent into a Scarlet Valkyrie.
__TOC__

sections.heading: Overview
sections.markdown:
All sisters can be found in Elphael, Brace of the Haligtree towards the end of Millicent's questline.
To reach them the player needs to:
- 1. Retrieve the snapped Unalloyed Gold Needle by defeating Commander O'Neil in the Heart of Aeonia.
 - Optional: Polyanna, Adopted Daughter can be summoned as a cooperator to assist in this fight.
- 2. Give the snapped needle to Sage Gowry at Gowry's Shack so that he may repair it.
- 3. Reload the area by either:
 - A. Resting at/teleporting to a Site of Grace
 - B. Exit to the Main Menu and then enter back into the game.
- 4. Retrieve the repaired needle from Gowry and then give it to Millicent at the Church of the Plague.
- 5. Reload the area by resting or teleporting to a grace then exhaust the dialogue of the now lucid Millicent.
- 6. Reload once more so Millicent moves to Gowry's Shack then exhaust her dialogue there.
 - Optional: The player may now summon Millicent to assist in the fight against Magma Wyrm Makar in Ruin-Strewn Precipice.
- 7. Defeat the Godskin Apostle at the peak of Dominula, Windmill Village.
 - Optional: Millicent can be summoned as a cooperator to assist in this fight.
- 8. Reload the area so Millicent may appear at the top of the Windmill Village and exhaust her dialogue.
 - Optional: The player may now summon Millicent to assist in the fight against the Draconic Tree Sentinel in Capital Outskirts.
 - Optional: The player may also summon Millicent to assist in the fight against the Black Blade Kindred in the Forbidden Lands.
- 9. Millicent will now appear by the Ancient Snow Valley Ruins Site of Grace at Mountaintops of the Giants. Exhaust her dialogue there.
- 10. Millicent will next appear by the Prayer Room site of grace in the beginning of Elphael, Brace of the Haligtree. Exhaust her dialogue there.
- 11. Defeat the Putrid Tree Spirit found in the isolated pool of Scarlet Rot just before the Drainage Channel site of grace in Elphael.
 - Optional: Players may talk to Sage Gowry at this time to unlock another option for the next step in Millicent's Quest.
- 12. One/Two summon signs will appear on a hill next to the pool of rot. The player may chose one to influence the end of Millicent's questline.
 - A. Assist Millicent: Accepting the Gold Sign will summon the player to help defend Millicent against her sisters. Failing in this task by either the player or Millicent dying will send the player back to their own world but allows them to retry assisting her or change to the other side. Succeeding in this task will reward the player with the Rotten Winged Sword Insignia and then the purified Unalloyed Gold Needle.
 - B. Challenge Millicent: Accepting the Red Sign will summon the player to help the sisters in killing Millicent. The player dying to Millicent will send them back to their own world but allows them to retry their attempt of killing her or change to the other option of assisting her. Succeeding in this task will reward the player with the Millicent's Prosthesis talisman.

sections.heading: Details
sections.markdown:
Unlike her sisters Polyanna can be encountered long before the confrontation at Elphael.

She can be summoned within the Swamp of Aeonia as a friendly cooperator against Commander O'Neil to help retrieving the snapped needle for Gowry.

Her Summon sign can be found directly south of the Inner Aeonia site of grace, en-caved among the tall roots of the Aeonia flower that are erupting directly up from the ground.

sections.heading: Polyanna's Appearance
sections.markdown:
Polyanna has a slender body, fair skin and the left half of her face is covered with a large, sickly birthmark.

Her right eye is covered with a white eye-patch and her visible left eye reveal that they are slightly clouded with a golden-yellow iris and a darkened, near-black sclerae.

She has faded orange-red hair tied into a bun at the back of her head, her forehead is covered with bangs that have been cut horizontally at the height of her eyebrows, along with thinner bangs on the sides reaching down to the height her chin.

sections.heading: Amy's Appearance
sections.markdown:
Amy has a slender body, fair skin and the upper half of her face from the top of her cheeks to her forehead, is covered with a large, sickly birthmark.

She has small pursed lips and both of her eyes are covered with a white blindfold. Despite not being visible, her eyes share the same features as Polyanna.

She has a faded orange-red, unkempt hair that reaches down to her shoulders, enveloping most of her whole head and even the right side of her face.

sections.heading: Maureen's Appearance
sections.markdown:
Maureen has a slender body, fair skin and the upper-left half of her face is covered with a large, sickly birthmark.

Her left eye is covered with a white eye-patch and her visible right eye reveal that her sclerae is also darkened like her sisters however unlike them, her iris and pupils are almost completely clouded over.

She has chin-length, curvaceous, faded orange-red hair covering most of her head. An opening revealing her face beginning on the right side of her forehead before curtaining out to the sides. where they eventually begin flowing back in towards the cheeks to then finally curve back outwards to the sides.

sections.heading: Mary's Appearance
sections.markdown:
Mary has a slender body, fair skin and the upper half of her face, from the top of her right cheek to the left-side top of her forehead is covered with a large, sickly birthmark.

She has both of her eyes are covered with a white blindfold. Despite not being visible, her eyes share the same features as Polyanna and Amy.

She has long faded orange-red hair that reaches down to her collar bone, an opening beginning on the upper left side of her face before curtaining outwards into large fluffy bangs framing her face.

sections.heading: Tactics
sections.markdown:
Successfully assisting Millicent can be accomplished with relative ease even with a character that hasn't leveled any of their attributes or weapons yet, as Millicent herself is significantly more powerful than any of the sisters individually. Her damage is high but her health is relatively low, so Millicent's safety is at the most risk only when she's greatly outnumbered and the majority of her sisters are attacking her at once.

Due to Millicent's high damage (particularly from her Waterfowl Dance), the player can equip the Shabriri's Woe Talisman and/or any pieces of the Duelist Set or Rotten Duelist Set to make the majority of the sisters more easily prone to chase them around the environment, leaving Millicent to deal with a single sister one at a time.

]]
Since Polyanna can cast Pest Threads, she's the only one who can harm the running player from a distance and so it's preferable to leave her with Millicent first so she can eliminate Polyanna before she becomes a problem for the player.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.markdown:
- Maureen's Treespear is unique and impossible to replicate by the player as it has Charge Forth. Instead the version the player has access to cannot be infused with Ashes of War and it has Sacred Order as it's default skill.
- It's possible to infer that Millicent may be the fourth sister to sprout from the Heart of Aeonia due to the fact that Polyanna is still present in Caelid at the start of the questline while her older sisters are comparatively absent, due to them likely having a head start on their journey to the Haligtree as they would have been born earlier than both Millicent and Polyanna.
- Since Malenia and Millicent can both blossom into giant flowers on death, it brings into question the large flower found in a chamber near the Haligtree Roots site of grace. It is unclear whether this is an earlier bloom from Malenia herself, as a copy of the Traveler's Set that can be found next to it may imply it is from one of the four sisters. However considering how much higher Gowry seems to value what Millicent's potential flower is likely going to be compared to her sisters, it may be from a sister we haven't heard of before.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.markdown: - Millicent's Sisters had different nameplates in : **Amy, Third Daughter**, **Mary, Eldest Daughter**, **Maureen, Second Daughter**, and **Polyanna, Youngest Daughter**.

sections.heading: Etymology
sections.markdown:
- ***Polyanna*** is derived from a combination of the names *Polly* (which in of itself has roots from the name *Mary*) and can mean "sea" and *Anna* (Derived from the Hebrew name *Hannah*, meaning "grace").
 - "Polyanna" has also been historically used as noun to describe an excessively cheerful or optimistic person. Stemming from the name of a character created by US writer of children's stories, *Eleanor Hodgman Porter*.
- ***Amy*** stems from French and means "beloved" or "well-loved". It's derived from the Latin word "amare" which in of itself means "to love".
- ***Maureen*** and ***Mary's*** names both stem from the same Hebrew name *Miriam*. It can translate to "drop of the sea", "bitterness", "beloved" and "wish for a child".

sections.heading: Summary
sections.markdown: Messmer the Impaler** (串刺し公、メスメル, *Kushizashi Kō, Mesumeru*), later known as **Base Serpent Messmer** (邪な蛇、メスメル, *Yokoshimana Hebi, Mesumeru*), is a mandatory remembrance boss in Shadow of the Erdtree.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.markdown:
Messmer is a Demigod who is encountered in the Shadow Keep. He is the source of Messmerfire and the Messmer's Flame incantations.

Messmer is **not** an optional boss as he must be defeated in order to acquire Messmer's Kindling that would allow the burning of the Sealing Tree at the Church of the Bud.

sections.heading: Background
sections.markdown:
Messmer was born to Queen Marika the Eternal prior to the Second Liurnian War. His birth was cursed by a dark entity, an evil serpent coiled within that threatened to subsume him. Known to Messmer as the Abyssal Serpent, this force was restrained only through Marika's intervention—she removed her son's right eye and replaced it with a seal of her Grace. Ever since his accursed birth, Messmer was in constant company of the winged serpents, friends who suppressed the base serpent.

Much like his younger sister, Messmer bore a vision of fire. and he despised the flame inside himself, and time and time again hoped to rid himself of it, but found that it ever burned.

At some point, Messmer befriended Commander Gaius, an Albinauric who, like him, was cursed from birth and akin to an older brother to General Radahn, Gaius' fellow student in the art of gravitational sorcery. Gaius would go on to command Messmer's armies during the crusade.

sections.heading: The Crusade
sections.markdown:
Toward the end of the Age of Plenty, Messmer was charged by his mother with carrying out a purge of the tower-dwelling hornsent of the Land of Shadow, who did not bear the light of grace. At some point during his Crusade, Messmer was abandoned in the Land of Shadow, but continued to zealously enforce the purge even though Marika used him as a scapegoat and ceased all contact with him. Messmer came to reside in a fort known as the Shadow Keep.

Key in his army were the Black Knights, commanded by Black Knight Commander Andreas and his son and second-in-command Black Knight Captain Huw. Although they remained devoutly loyal to Messmer despite his abandonment by Marika, they ultimately rebelled upon learning of his serpentine nature. The pair were imprisoned in an underground tomb, and despite his betrayal, Messmer mourned the loss of Huw, whom he had considered a brother-in-arms. His Fire Knights would also refuse to follow the orders of burning the Ancient Ruins of Rauh and the destruction of the specimens in the Specimen Storehouse.

Eventually, an intruder invaded Messmer's stronghold, the Shadow Keep, and was noticed by the demigod's serpents, who identified them as a Tarnished Champion and a pretender to the title of Elden Lord. Though surprised that a Tarnished had come to the Land of Shadow, Messmer nonetheless attacked them to continue enforcing the purge. However, the serpentine demigod struggled overcome the Tarnished. Unwilling to accept "a Lord devoid of light" and desperate to regain the upper hand, Messmer ripped out Marika's seal and unleashed the power of the Abyssal Serpent, allowing him to frequently transform into a massive serpent. Nonetheless, the Tarnished was able to land a fatal blow upon Messmer. Realizing that his mother had indeed forsaken him, Messmer used his dying breath to curse Marika.

sections.heading: Boss Fight
sections.markdown: Hornsent can be summoned for this boss. His summon sign is found inside of the boss room, and will appear if the player decides to side with him against Leda or ignore this part of Leda's quest.

sections.heading: Phase One
sections.markdown:
The attacks of **Messmer the Impaler** are imbued with fire damage, making him a formidable opponent who relies heavily on his spear's reach and agility. To proceed in this boss fight, readiness for his swift movements is important. When fighting Messmer at a close range, you will have more chances of retaliating and chipping away at his health while he recovers. Engaging Messmer patiently is the best strategy to effectively take him down. When he finishes a string of attacks, focus on breaking his poise by pulling off heavy attacks for a chance to deal significant damage.

Because of his speed, Messmer can quickly transition between offense and defense by quickly disengaging with a leap after he finishes a move. Be aware that Messmer counters swiftly after sustaining damage, too. As his speed and precision in combat are his biggest asset, observation is required to avoid being overwhelmed. Once Messmer's health is half-depleted, a cutscene will trigger, which will start Messmer's second phase.

sections.heading: Phase Two
sections.markdown: During the second phase, **Base Serpent Messmer** remains at 50% HP and not only retains his original attacks, but also introduces a set of new and more lethal attacks with the help of the Abyssal Serpent. Among the fresh additions to his move set is the ability to transform into a large red serpent that rises up to the ground to throw a fireball or do bite attacks.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.markdown:
- Messmer was likely born earlier than the other Demigods. Exactly when he was born remains unknown, as all mention of him was erased by his mother after she abandoned him in the Land of Shadow.
 - He is older than Radahn, who was born before Miquella, Malenia, Trina, and Ranni.
- Although not explicitly stated, Messmer is strongly implied to be an Empyrean child of Marika and Radagon, born of a single god.
 - Messmer has the red hair of Radagon and his children.
 - Messmer was cursed at birth by a threat to Marika's power.
 - Radagon's motif in *The Final Battle* is echoed in the soundtrack for Messmer's boss fight, *Messmer the Impaler*.
 - Messmer is linked to Black Pyreflies, one of four butterflies found in-game, two of which are associated with Empyreans born from a single god. The Smoldering Butterflies correspond with Melina.
 - Seals are placed on his eyes.
- Messmer is the elder brother of Melina, as both she and his younger sister were daughters of Marika with visions of fire.
 - Melina serves as kindling to burn the Erdtree, and Messmer's Kindling can burn the Sealing Tree.
 - Melina, who has a corresponding butterfly and faded red hair, must also be an Empyrean child of Marika-Radagon because the game makes the distinction that Messmer and Radahn, his half-brother, are not brothers; Messmer acted like an elder brother to Radahn, but was not one.
- Upon his defeat, Messmer denounces Marika and curses her with his dying breath. This is the only time he refers to his mother by name.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.markdown:
- Messmer's name may be a nod to German physician Franz Mesmer, who theorized about the existence of "animal magnetism" (a universal, invisible force or "magnetic fluid" that he supposed connected all living things and was capable of curing diseases, later referred to as *mesmerism*). Mesmerism would eventually come to be associated with hypnosis and is today considered a synonym for the former (with the term "mesmerizing" coined after it).
- Messmer's epithet is most likely inspired by Vlad III, commonly known as "Vlad the Impaler" (Romanian: *Vlad Țepeș*; rendered in Japanese as "串刺し公" (*Kushizashi Kō*)), who was one of the historical inspirations for Bram Stoker's novel **. Like Vlad III, Messmer has a notable draconic motif: while "Dracula" means "son of the dragon" (Vlad's father was called Vlad Dracul), Messmer for his part wears a helm shaped like a dragon's head, dons armor resembling the Drake Knight set, and has a snake with dragon wings.
- Messmer's visual design was likely inspired by the marble sculpture of Laocoön and His Sons, which depicts a pair of serpents winding circuitously around a priest and his sons, whose divine punishment for attempting to destroy the Trojan Horse and expose the trap is misinterpreted by the Trojans as proof that Laocoön was the real traitor and that the horse was trustworthy. This sculpture is famous for being one of the greatest examples of dynamic motion and emotion of its time.
- Messmer has an unused voice line that would have played during the cinematic for his boss fight. He would have told the Tarnished, *"Miquella spoke of thee..."*

sections.heading: Summary
sections.markdown: Needle Knight Leda** is an NPC in *Elden Ring: Shadow of the Erdtree*.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.markdown:
The last member of the Needle Knights, an order devoted to Miquella of the Haligtree. Leda was guided by Miquella to the Realm of Shadow alongside her compatriots, all of whom were under the influence of a powerful charm which compelled them to follow the Empyrean. While in the Realm of Shadow, Leda followed the trail of crosses left by Miquella, discovering in the process that he sought the Gate of Divinity, which was sealed away by a tree.

The Tarnished encounters Leda in Mohgwyn Palace, where she urges them to touch the withered arm in Miquella's cocoon to enter the Realm of Shadow. Within the Land of Shadow, the Tarnished meets Leda and her various compatriots on their search for Miquella, seeking out the crosses to ascertain his route. However, the charm inflicted upon the compatriots is broken when Miquella's Great Rune is shattered. Leda's devotion to Miquella is unshaken, but she begins to suspect her compatriots of disloyalty. Leda sets about ferreting out those she believes undeserving of a place at Miquella's side, with her potential targets being the Hornsent and Sir Ansbach. The Tarnished may assist her in her hunt, or side with her opponents.

After gaining access to Enir-Ilim, the Tarnished encounters Leda for a final time on the way to the Gate of Divinity. Leda deduces that the Tarnished was never guided by Miquella, and concludes that they were instead following the guidance of the Erdtree. Viewing the Tarnished as a threat to Miquella's ascension, she challenges them. The Tarnished triumphs over Leda and her remaining allies, and continues to the top of the tower.

sections.heading: Questline Progression
sections.markdown:
1. Defeat both Starscourge Radahn and Mohg, Lord of Blood. Then rest on the nearest Site of Grace. Leda will appear in front of Miquella's cocoon at Mohgywn Dynasty Mausoleum and urge to interact with it.

2. Defeat the Divine Beast Dancing Lion, climb up the stairs in the adjacent room and collect the item on the top; a letter from Leda.

3. Defeat Rellana, Twin Moon Knight, Leda can be summoned for this fight. After the fight, you can find Leda again in the next Site of Grace.

4. Return to the same place and speak to Leda after visiting the entrance of the Shadow Keep.

5. Speaking with Leda and choose an option:

- Suggest Thiollier -> Nothing happens?
- Suggest Hornsent -> She goes after Hornsent
- Suggest no one -> she goes after Hornsent
Rest on the site of grace and speak with Leda again after choosing an option.

6. (If she goes after Hornsent) you can find a summon signs in the Shadow Keep.

7. She can be found at the Storehouse, First Floor where Sir Ansbach is.

8. Regardless of any choices made, Leda will be finally found at Enir Ilim, where she will be waiting for a quick chat with the player.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.markdown: Metyr, Mother of Fingers** is an optional Remembrance Boss in Elden Ring, introduced in the Shadow of the Erdtree expansion.

sections.heading: Background
sections.markdown:
Metyr, the brilliant daughter of the Greater Will, was the first of all stars to fall upon the Lands Between. She possessed a microcosm which allowed her to receive messages from the Greater Will. Metyr gave birth to the Two Fingers that guided the empyreans and the Tarnished.

Long ago, Metyr was damaged and her Ringed Finger was removed. She would never again receive a signal from the Greater Will. The wisdom received by the Two Fingers was severed, and Metyr began birthing the aberrant Fingercreepers. Metyr concealed herself within the Finger Ruins of Miyr, below the Cathedral of Manus Metyr, and waited for an eternity in vain for another signal from her lord.

Although Metyr was broken, her Two Fingers continued guiding the empyreans without a word from the Greater Will. It is said they presided over the birth of Marika’s Erdtree as she created it from the primordial matter of the Crucible.

sections.heading: Characteristics
sections.markdown:
Metyr is a monstrous being made from fingers. Her head resembles an elongated thumb, and her face a pronounced thumbprint. At its center is a small, wart-like eye from which she blasts pink energy beams. Ridge-like wrinkles, forming fingerprint-like patterns, cover Metyr's head and neck. She moves about on four sets of four-fingered hands, 16 coordinated finger legs in total. Metyr has two long-reaching arms that terminate in four-fingered hands tipped with sharp nails painted red. She may use these to pry open her abdominal cavity when birthing new Fingercreepers. Her tail forks into two tail fingers which wrap each other like a spiral. Between them rests an orb containing a microcosm.

Metyr's body festers with unhealed wounds. Upon her right chest is a deep laceration, and her belly has been split wide open, revealing gore and the stillborn remains of malformed fingers. Several more protrude from large lesions on her neck and tail fingers, and her microcosm appears clouded like an eye with cataracts. The iris of her bloodshot eye is quartered into a quatrefoil.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.markdown:
- Metyr, Mother of Fingers deals Standard, Strike, Pierce, Magic, and Holy damage
- She is resistant to Magic, Fire, Lightning and Holy damage. She is immune to Sleep, Madness, and Death Blight.
- Her weaknesses are Slash damage and Blood Loss.

sections.markdown:

This area becomes accessible after advancing Count Ymir's questline. To reach it, the player must ring the two hanging bells at the other Finger Ruins, return to the cathedral, examine Ymir's throne, and descend the newly revealed ladder to the ruins below. There, they must defeat Swordhand of Night Anna before ringing the final bell.

- The many fingers protruding from Metyr's wounds resemble Festering Bloody Fingers. There are several different models, but they typically only have one or two fingers.

sections.markdown: Midra, Lord of Frenzied Flame**, also known as **Sage Midra**, is an optional boss in Shadow of the Erdtree.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.markdown:
Long ago, the great Sage Midra attempted to become a Lord of Frenzied Flame. However, he was too weak and failed. Pierced by the branching thorns of the Greatsword of Damnation, his power was suppressed by the hornsent. Midra's Manse and the dark lands of the Abyssal Woods were forbidden by the Hornsent. It is said the eyes of those who served the sage were burned by the Frenzied Flame of madness. Midra lingered on in perpetual suffering at the behest of his beloved Nanaya.

Eventually, a Tarnished Champion entered Midra's manse to explore and loot it. Midra repeatedly tried to warn the Tarnished to leave, but his pleas went unheeded. Upon the Tarnished coming upon Midra's chambers, Midra chastised the Tarnished for their foolishness before attacking them, only to be brutally beaten and subdued. Finally, Midra could endure his pain no more. He pulls the sword out through his head and decapitates himself. Then, he manifests as the Lord of Frenzied Flame. The branching arms of the sword coil tightly around its central needle.

sections.heading: Appearance
sections.markdown: A feeble man wearing a yellow or gold robe with a large clasp with green gems. A golden stake is driven through his eye that continues into his body. Its barbs emerge from his torso in the shape of an evergreen. He unseals the Frenzied Flame by removing the rod through his eye, decapitating himself to reveal a gazing fireball of Frenzied Flame. The barbs coil around the weapon to form his sword.

sections.markdown: - You fight the feeble Lord. He is easily staggered and has low health compared to his actual fight, but can still prove dangerous with a scream AoE or grab attack if not dealt with quickly.

sections.heading: Phase One

sections.heading: Phase Two
sections.markdown: - When Midra's health drops to about 65%, he will rise up above you and drop down for a massive explosion. After that, Midra will retain his original strings of attacks and will gain new ones that more frequently utilize madness.

sections.heading: Effect
sections.markdown:
Creates a miniature Minor Erdtree at the caster's feet for 30 seconds.

Caster and nearby allies are healed for 18 HP every 0.5 seconds (1070 HP total over the entire duration) as long as the effect remains active.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.markdown:
- Area of effect is roughly 3-4 times larger than the visual effect, presumably due to the size of the spell's visual being changed before release (see trivia).
- Generally outclassed by other healing incantations such as Great Heal or Blessing's Boon, as those like the former heal immediately while those like the latter do not require characters to stay in a small area to be healed.
- Duration is NOT affected by the Old Lord's Talisman.
- Deals damage equal to 10 + 3% of their health to Revenants and Revenant Followers for every second they are in the effect radius of the spell.
- Compared to Warming Stones: same duration (30 seconds), more healing per second (effectively 36 HP per seconds vs 25 HP per seconds) and total healing (1070 HP vs 720 HP), costs more FP (30 FP vs 20 FP), and takes 70 Faith and 2 Spell slots instead of needing to be crafted. It also has the difference of not healing nearby enemies, unlike Warming Stones, and only 10 Warming Stones can be carried at a time.
 - The comparison with Sunwarmth Stones is slightly closer as it increases slightly (30 HP per second, or 900 total HP over the duration), in exchange for taking slightly more FP to cast (24) and requiring more rare materials to craft. Duration and healing even enemies remain the same for Sunwarmth Stones.
- Compared to Frenzyflame Stones: same duration (30 seconds), slightly more healing per second (effectively 36 HP per seconds vs 35 HP per seconds) and total healing (1070 HP vs 1050 HP), costs more FP (30 FP vs 15 FP), and takes 70 Faith and 2 Spell slots instead of needing to be crafted. The Frenzyflame Stones additionally only heal players that are attuned to the Frenzied Flame.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.markdown:
- Patch 1.13 increased HP recovery amount.
 - Technically it lowered the amount of HP healed per tick, from 24 to 18, but since it also decreased the interval between heals from 1 second to 0.5 seconds the amount healed was effectively increased by 49%.
- A version of this spell that summons a significantly larger tree is used by Melina when summoned against Morgott, the Omen King.
- The size of the summoned tree was greatly decreased from the preview of Elden Ring: Shadow of the Erdtree, allegedly because its original size made it cause significant slowdown of the game when summoned.
- Has the second highest Faith requirement for an incantation, surpassed only by Light of Miquella.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.markdown: Midra's Flame of Frenzy** is an incantation spell in Shadow of the Erdtree. It is one of the Three Fingers Incantations.

sections.heading: Acquisition
sections.markdown:
Trade:** Remembrance of the Lord of Frenzied Flame
- Exchange the Remembrance with Finger Reader Enia at Roundtable Hold.
 - The remembrance is acquired by defeating Midra, Lord of Frenzied Flame.
 - After the Remembrance is acquired, a Wandering Mausoleum or Remembrance Duplication Coffins can be used to duplicate it. The spell can only be acquired once per new game cycle, regardless of how many remembrances are held.

sections.heading: Effect
sections.markdown:
Summons an orb of Frenzied Flame that shoots out bolts of flame in front of the caster, dealing Fire damage equal to 75% of Incantation Scaling and inflicting 30 Madness build-up per hit.

The caster suffers 6 Madness build-up 7 times per second, and any enemy within 5 meters of the orb takes 10 Madness build-up 2.5 times per second.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.markdown:
- Inflicts a lot of Madness build-up on the caster, enough to fully inflict the status effect in less than 10 seconds, necessitating high amounts of Focus to use this spell effectively.
- Madness build-up scales with the Arcane-scaling of the Dragon Communion Seal.
- Damage is boosted by 20% per Frenzied Flame Seal held in an active hand (2 max).
- Very effective for keeping the damage boosts from Black Dumpling, Aged One's Exultation, and Madding Hand active during combat.
- More effective when cast under foes that are large enough that the orb is summoned inside of them.
- Drains FP much quicker when channeled than the additional cost of 5 would imply, as it drains 7 times per second (or 35 FP per seconds).
- Can move when casting and can be cast while riding Torrent.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.markdown:
- The summoned orb is similar to the orb that replaces The Tarnished's head during the Lord of Frenzied Flame ending.
- Patch 1.14 increased attack speed, increased Frenzy status buildup range against enemies, decreased Frenzy status buildup when using this skill.
 - The self-Madness build-up was reduced from 7 build-up per tick to 6 build-up per tick.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.markdown: Messmer's Orb** is an incantation spell in Shadow of the Erdtree. It's one of the Messmer's Flame Incantations.

sections.heading: Acquisition
sections.markdown:
Trade:** Remembrance of the Impaler
- Exchange the Remembrance with Finger Reader Enia at Roundtable Hold.
 - The remembrance is acquired by defeating Midra, Lord of Frenzied Flame.
 - After the Remembrance is acquired, a Wandering Mausoleum or Remembrance Duplication Coffins can be used to duplicate it. The spell can only be acquired once per new game cycle, regardless of how many remembrances are held.

sections.heading: Effect
sections.markdown:
Caster jumps into the air and then dashes forwards to their target, burning them with Fire Attack Power equal to 50% of Incantation Scaling upon contact when flying and 308% of the same when the orb explodes.

If charged, contact Attack Power increases to 70% of Incantation Scaling and explosion Attack Power to 411% of the same.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.markdown:
- Attack Power is boosted by 15% by the Godfrey Icon if charged.
 - Since charging the spell already increases contact Attack Power by 40% and explosion Attack Power by 33%, wearing this talisman increases contact Attack Power by 61% and explosion Attack Power by 53%.
- Attack Power is boosted by 15% per Fire Knight Seal held in an active hand (2 max).
- Attack Power is boosted by 3% when the Messmer's Helm is worn.
- Attack Power is boosted by 4% when the Fire Knight Armor is worn.
- The caster isn't granted any amount of Hyperarmor when mid-air, making their speed and maneuverability the only thing that keeps them from being knocked out of the spell.
- Best used at medium range since it makes it harder for enemies to interrupt. Using it at melee range has the additional danger of making its maneuverability hard to control and therefore risking that it overshoots the target.
